title: Plugin that can allow for surprise attacks

posts.author: MythrilKnight
posts.body: I need a plugin or something similar that can allow for pre-emptive attacks when the player gets the enemy from behind, akin to the Romancing SaGa games, and for the inverse to be true. I'm using RPG Maker MZ for my game.

posts.author: coucassi
posts.body:
VisuStellas Encounter Effects
has this function.
EDIT: Oh wait, it's not free. I'm still living in the old days, before yanfly.moe put up the paywall >.<
Might still be worth it, if you are willing to spend the money, since it has a lot of other useful functions too.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body: My big-box-of-stuff plugin, Cae_Tweaks, has 2 features that I think could achieve this: M32 - event notetag stops event from facing player when triggered. You can check player and/or event direction with a Conditional Branch. D12 - lets you force surprise/preemptive via plugin commands. MZ - Cae_Tweaks - lots of little features Cae_Tweaks v19 updated 2026-06-16 (UTC+0) Terms of Use MIT License: https://opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.html Description The plugin file must be named Cae_Tweaks.js. This plugin contains a bunch of different things. It's mostly just me slowly making a game and coding some more stuff... forums.rpgmakerweb.com There are probably other options, e.g. Galv's Event Utility lets you check how an event was started, which might be more convenient in your case: MZ Event Utility – Galv's RPG Maker Scripts & Plugins MZ PLUGINS - Cam Control MZ - Move Route Extras MZ -

posts.author: coucassi
posts.body:
Is the trap in a fix location, or is the player able to set the trap anywhere on the map? If it's on a fixed location, you could use a parallel event to check if the monsters coordinates are matching this location and then turn a switch on.
If the trap has multiple possible locations, you'd have the event check if the coordinates of both events match, before turning the switch.

Oh, now I understood what you mean. Then you need to do something like
@coucassi
said.
An easy way to check for there is more than one event in a map coordinate is this:
$gameMap.eventsXy(10, 20).length >= 2
Replace 10 and 20 for x and y respectivelly.
But that will not check the event id. It can be any event id.
Another way would be:
$gameMap.event(ID1).pos(x, y)
Replacing X and Y for the location you want to check and DI1 for the event ID you want to check
That would work for you?
